text:
Sam Reinhart turned 31 on Nov. 6 with two Stanley Cups and a reputation as one of Florida's most complete forwards. Eighteen games in, the scoring line is close to normal: 17 points, 9 goals, 9 power-play points, about 20 minutes a night.

The chances say he should have more. He has 10.75 expected goals (the quality of his shots), well up from his rate last season, and he has scored 9. That is a player getting to the right ice; Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 1.8 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net last season.

What is worrying is the five-on-five picture. The Panthers out-shoot opponents with him on the ice, but they get only 45.7% of the expected goals, 8.5 points worse than without him. He was already facing the other team's best last season, 97th percentile in competition by Evolving-Hockey. Florida lost three of its last four, and we'd watch whether his line starts tilting the ice back.
headline: Reinhart is getting chances, but not the territory
